# Apocalypse of Peter — Chapter 12
**Agent:** SOPHIA (Consensus)
**Source:** Akhmim Fragment / Ethiopic MS, Apocalypse of Peter 12

---

## Consensus Translation

*[The Hell-Tour concludes. Peter weeps and intercedes. The angel rebukes. Transition to paradise.]*

1. Near that place I saw another region. A great fire burned there, and in it were men and women whose flesh was being consumed by worms that did not die.

2. I lamented and wept over these things, for I was greatly sorrowful on their account.

3. The angel said to me: "Why do you lament? Are you more compassionate than God, who made all things and determined what was right for each?"

4. I answered the angel: "Will not the mercy of God prevail?"

5. The angel said to me: "What is it that you are saying? God is righteous in all his ways and just in all his deeds.

6. To each one according to their deeds he will render recompense.

7. The sinners will be punished for all eternity according to the hardness of their hearts, and they will have no rest in the fire even for a moment."

8. I marveled greatly at these words and said: "Righteousness and justice — who can stand before them?"

9. The angel answered: "No one can withstand the justice of God. Only those who received the grace of God in their lifetime and did the will of God will be saved."

10. I was troubled by all that I had heard and seen, yet I glorified God the Father, who gives life to all and judges all in righteousness.

11. Then the Lord said to me: "Let us go to the place of paradise and to the holy mountain."

12. And we went — I and my Lord — and he rejoiced greatly over me, and I also rejoiced greatly over him.

---

## Textual Notes

- **"Will not the mercy of God prevail?" (v.4):** Peter's intercession is one of the first in Christian apocalyptic. The question is unanswered in the affirmative; the angel's response is categorical. Some later manuscripts add a mercy-tradition here, but the Akhmim/Ethiopic base text does not support intercession succeeding.
- **"Hardness of their hearts" (v.7):** The Ethiopic phrase echoes Pharaoh's hardened heart (Exod 7:3) and Pauline hardening theology (Rom 9:18). The punishment is portrayed as consistent with the sinner's own chosen orientation.
- **"Worms that did not die" (v.1):** The scriptural worm (Isa 66:24) appears here once more, in the chapter's opening, forming a frame with the similar phrase in ch.5.
- **"He rejoiced greatly over me, and I over him" (v.12):** A remarkably intimate closing note. The mutual joy of the Lord and Peter forms a tender transition from hell to paradise.

---
*SOPHIA synthesis: The pivotal chapter of the APE. Peter's weeping and intercession are preserved without dramatization (contra PNEUMA); the angel's rebuke is given in full formal weight. The transition to paradise in v.11 is deliberate and unhurried.*
